An inter - BAPS Chhatralay Convention commenced from today wherein sadhus and Swamishri inspired students through enlightening lectures and blessings.

ds.t: Rejoice in a crowd of devotees
w: Some satsangis get tired of the crowds of devotees in the mandir, and that is why they avoid coming to the mandir for darshan. During Pramukh Swami Maharaj's meetings at Edison in New Jersey, just such a son of a staunch satsangi came. The sadhus said to Swamishri, "He comes for darshan but does not come to the assembly. When we tell him, he says he does not like crowds."

Hearing this, Swamishri lovingly said to him, "What crowds there are all over America! If there is a crowd in your store too, do you go back home, or are you pleased to see the crowd? In the same way, rejoice in this crowd of devotees. So you must come to the satsang assembly at the mandir."

Prabhashankarbhai Pandya of Ahmedabad, now living in America, is a long-standing and devoted satsangi from the time of Shastriji Maharaj. On 24 May 2004, during the evening meal in Edison, Prabhashankarbhai recalled many memories of Shastriji Maharaj. Along with them he also told some incidents of Pramukh Swami Maharaj.

Recalling one memory, he said, "Shastriji Maharaj was in Atladra. Arjun Kaka and Shastriji Maharaj were talking all about the gateway at Sarangpur. Motibhai was also standing beside them. Motibhai was the father of Pramukh Swami Maharaj before he became a sadhu.
"Pointing to Motibhai, Shastriji Maharaj asked Arjunbhai, 'Do you know this devotee?'

"'He has given us a son with thirty-six qualities.' Shastriji Maharaj said this while introducing Motibhai. I too was standing beside them. I thought to myself, what does thirty-six qualities mean? So when Shastriji Maharaj had finished talking and was a little more relaxed, I asked, 'Swami! The scriptures speak of thirty qualities and sixty-four qualities, but what does thirty-six qualities mean?'
"Then Shastriji Maharaj said, 'You know that a sadhu has thirty qualities, don't you!'
"'Yes, Swami!'

"'Well, this Narayanda (Shastriji Maharaj called Pramukh Swami Maharaj, that is Narayanswarupdasji, by this pet name) has those thirty qualities of a sadhu, but in addition he will act like a king of kings.'
"So I requested, 'Please show me that.'

"Shastriji Maharaj said, 'You will get to see it.' And today I am seeing this satsang in America. The way satsang is growing across the whole world, what Shastriji Maharaj said I am now seeing with my own eyes."
Saying this much, Prabhashankarbhai was choked with emotion. Then, unfolding more of his memories, he went on:

"There was the Vasant Panchami festival in Atladra. It was the cold season. I arrived late at night. Everyone had gone to sleep. Not finding a place to stay or any bedding anywhere, I lay down near the steps in the assembly hall, using my bag as a pillow. In the morning at about 5.30, Pragat Bhagat came to me. He woke me up and said, 'Pandya, get up!'
"When I woke up with a start, there was a quilt over my body. I asked, 'Who put this quilt over me?'
"Then Pragat Bhagat said, 'Pramukh Swami Maharaj came at night and put his own quilt over you.'
"Truly, seeing his saintliness and the way he valued devotees, one is choked with emotion."

For the evening parayan (discourse) a pothi-yatra (procession of scripture) was carried out with festivity. The parayan was to be held in memory of the late Dineshbhai (Gadhadi).

In the evening assembly, Viveksagar Swami conducted the parayan of Shri Harililakalpataru. Thereafter a welcome dance was performed by the local youths. Finally, in his blessings Swamishri talked about the Harililakalpataru scripture which describes the supreme glory of Bhagwan Swaminarayan. “The amrut (immortalising nectar) is found in the world of gods. But that amrut cannot help you transcend maya. The material pleasures of swarg are not everlasting. When one’s merits are exhausted one has to come back to mrutyulok (earth). The divine nectar of God dissolves our base nature and properties of maya within and blesses us with God’s eternal abode…”

In the evening the assembly celebrating Yogiji Maharaj’s 114th birthday was addressed by different sadhus lauding the virtues of Yogiji Maharaj on the theme “Vani amrutthi bhari madhu sami...” Thereafter Viveksagar Swami addressed the assembly. After a traditional dance by BAPS children and youths Swamishri blessed the devotees, “Yogiji Maharaj had countless virtues. Whatever has been written in the shastras about saintliness, one finds them in the life of Yogiji Maharaj. There was no maya or mundaneness in him. He saw only God in all. We talk about the Gunatit state, but we could see it entirely in Yogiji Maharaj. He never thought or desired for glory, greatness, fame or to look nice before others. He was always humble and beheld all devotees and small children with glory...” Ten thousands devotees availed of the celebration.

At 10.45 am Swamishri performed the consecration rituals of murtis that would be adorned with clothes – Shri Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj, Shri Radha-Krishna Dev and small, delicate murtis of Guru Parampara in marble. An annakut of 1,151 vegetarian food items was offered to Thakorji. Swamishri performed the pratishtha rituals of pujan, arti and mantra pushpanjali.

In the pratishtha assembly Viveksagar Swami gave a brief history of Satsang in East Africa. Thereafter Swamishri blessed the congregation, “Today, the murti-pratishtha festival has been wonderfully accomplished for the third time. God is very merciful. Such occasions help to enhance our bhakti. Through genuine devotion God is pleased upon us. We have to consolidate God’s instructions and the philosophy of Akshar-Purushottam in our souls. Maharaj had accomplished a unique mission. Thereafter Shastriji Maharaj established the upasana of Akshar and Purushottam, and that God is one. We do not become God but forever remain his humble servant. No matter how intelligent one may be, no matter how wealthy one may be but one has to remain a humble servant.” In all 3,500 devotees and well wishers took mahaprasad.

The evening satsang assembly was dedicated to the celebration of Swamishri’s symbolic 60th anniversary as the president of the BAPS. Several sadhus narrated incidents about Swamishri’s saintliness and other virtues. Then a video on Swamishri was shown. Viveksagar Swami discoursed on Swamishri’s saintliness and Herculean efforts for the growth of Satsang. Thereafter, children and teenagers performed a traditional dance. Then a drama written by Adarshjivan Swami was enacted. The celebration assembly closed with Swamishri’s blessings, “We are all making efforts together in Satsang – youth volunteers, sadhus and devotees. I offer my vandan to all. I see in you all sentiments of dedication and sacrifice. The reason for this is that Yogiji Maharaj had visited here often, and blessed you with his divine joy, discourses and love. Whatever is accomplished in the Sanstha is due to the glory of Shastriji Maharaj and the wish of Yogiji Maharaj. Shriji Maharaj had said that without his will a dry leaf can not be moved.” Swamishri released a memorial publication, ‘Smruti’, depicting the history of Mumbai Satsang Mandal. Thereafter Swamishri was honoured with garlands and a flower shawl by senior sadhus.

A well known devotee came for darshan. He and his wife both have PhDs and are professors. They had come to get guidance from Pramukh Swami Maharaj on which line of study their son, who had reached Standard 12, should take. He said to Swamishri, "My wish is to make him a doctor. Even if he gets low marks, I will get him admission by paying a donation."
Swamishri said, "Not like that. What does the boy want to do?" Saying this, Swamishri asked his son, "What do you want to become?"
"I want to become an engineer."
Swamishri said, "Then let him go into what he has interest and liking for."

In today's times there are hundreds of cases of students who fall short of their parents' expectations and drop out of studies midway, or study unwillingly and ruin their lives, and finally even commit suicide. In this situation, Swamishri's guidance is practical and extremely useful.

Mansukhbhai Jani, a Brahmin devotee living in Mumbai, came for darshan. He had stayed in the service of Chunibhai Chaturvedi. He too is elderly. Today, when he came for Pramukh Swami Maharaj's darshan and Swamishri learnt that he had stayed in the service of Chunibhai Chaturvedi, Swamishri immediately gave him blessings of pleasure and said, "That you have served Chunibhai is a very great thing. Chunibhai served Yogiji Maharaj greatly and pleased him. You will gain great merit."
The joy seen on Swamishri's face as he said this was indescribable.
An MLA and members of his team came for darshan. One of the members said to Pramukh Swami Maharaj, "Please make the MLA give up his addiction."

Swamishri immediately said, "Society still needs you very much, so if you give up your addiction, you will be able to do even more seva. And when we hold a position, our very first task is to remove addictions from society. If addictions go from society, people will be happy. But before that we have to give them up ourselves, so you too should give it up."

ds.t: "The responsibility of this mandir is yours"
w: Pramukh Swami Maharaj met Mahendrasinh Jadeja, who had come from Dhrol. Mahendrasinh is connected with the Bilada state. He is the husband of Mohanba, the daughter of Diwan Saheb. He has had close ties with the organisation for the last 45 years. Yogiji Maharaj too visited his home many times. He has even carried Yogiji Maharaj's chair. Moreover, Yogiji Maharaj once said to him, "Since you are Dajibapu's son in law, you are our son in law too." He recalled all these memories before Swamishri. Although because of circumstances he had not been able to come into satsang, Swamishri remembered him again and again during the installation festival. He also gave him an invitation to come to the yagna, and in this way, out of affection, he called him today. He came. Swamishri met him lovingly. He had a chair placed in front of him and seated him, placed a garland on him and said to him, "You are a leader of Hindu society, and this mandir that has been built in Bhadra is also a mandir of the Hindu religion. Now the responsibility of protecting this mandir is yours."

Because of Swamishri's affection and the trust placed in him, he was choked with emotion and tears came to his eyes. Even after coming out, he reminded Dharmakunvar Swami of this ten times and said, "The responsibility of this mandir is mine." Swamishri's way of showing affection is unique.

Swamishri had specially sent for a shawl for him. Draping the shawl over him, Swamishri said, "I specially remembered you at the yagna, but you could not come, so today we are specially draping a shawl over you."

Pramukh Swami Maharaj had his farali meal. After finishing it, he addressed Shrijipriya Swami, one of the sadhus sitting in front, who has lived and served here for years, and said, "Liquor and gutkha (chewing tobacco) have crept into the village a great deal. So give everyone a niyam and explain to them that these are bad addictions. Money is wasted and health is ruined. If there is money, it will be useful. If the money goes, what will they do? So make a point of talking to everyone, and since the mandir has been built, give them the niyam of coming for darshan. Keep calling everyone and keep following up every day."

A well known devotee came for darshan. He and his wife both hold PhDs and are professors. They had come to seek Pramukh Swami Maharaj's guidance on which line of study their son, who had reached the twelfth standard, should take. He said to Swamishri, "My wish is to make him a doctor. Even if his marks are low, I will get him admission through a donation."
Swamishri said, "Not like that. What does the boy want to do?" Having said this, Swamishri asked his son, "What do you want to become?"
"I want to become an engineer."
Swamishri said, "Then let him go into whatever he has interest and liking for."

In today's times there are hundreds of cases of students who fall short of their parents' expectations and either drop their studies halfway, or study unwillingly and ruin their lives, and in the end even commit suicide. In this situation, Swamishri's guidance is practical and extremely useful.

Mansukhbhai Jani, a Brahmin devotee living in Mumbai, came for darshan. He had served Chunibhai Chaturvedi. He too is elderly, but today, when he came for Pramukh Swami Maharaj's darshan and Swamishri came to know that he had served Chunibhai Chaturvedi, Swamishri immediately gave him blessings of his pleasure, saying, "That you have served Chunibhai is a very great thing. Chunibhai served Yogiji Maharaj a great deal and pleased him. You will receive great merit."
The joy seen on Swamishri's face as he spoke like this was indescribable.
An MLA and the members of his team came for darshan. One of these members said to Pramukh Swami Maharaj, "Please get the MLA to give up his addiction."

Swamishri immediately said, "Society still needs you very much, so if you give up your addiction you can do even more seva, and when we hold a position, our very first task is to remove addiction from society. If addiction goes from society, people will become happy. But before that we have to give it up ourselves, so you too should give it up."

Pramukh Swami Maharaj met Mahendrasinh Jadeja, who had come from Dhrol. Mahendrasinh is connected with the Bilada State. He is the husband of Mohanba, daughter of the Diwan sahib. For the last 45 years he has had close ties with the organisation. Yogiji Maharaj had also visited his home many times. He had even carried Yogiji Maharaj's chair. Moreover, Yogiji Maharaj had once told him, "Dajibapu's son in law is our son in law." He recalled all these memories before Swamishri. Though due to circumstances he had not been able to come to satsang, Swamishri remembered him often during the installation festival. He also gave him an invitation to come to the yagna, and in this way, with affection, called him today. He came. Swamishri met him lovingly. He had a chair placed in front for him and seated him there, placed a garland on him, and said to him, "You are a leader of Hindu society, and this mandir that has been built in Bhadra is also a mandir of Hindu dharma. Now the responsibility of protecting this mandir is yours."

Moved by Swamishri's affection and the trust placed in him, he was choked with emotion, and tears came to his eyes. Even after coming out, he reminded Dharmakunvar Swami of this ten times and said, "The responsibility for this mandir is mine." Swamishri's way of showing love is unique.

Swamishri had specially sent for a shawl for him. Placing the shawl on him, Swamishri said, "I specially remembered you at the yagna, but you could not come, so today we are specially placing a shawl on you."

Mahant Swami Maharaj came to the Abhishek Mandapam. While he was having darshan of the mahapuja here, Kanubhai Patel (US), ringing the mahapuja bell, said, "We are ringing the bell by your command."
With a gesture of his hand, Swamishri said, "Then you are brahmarup."

While having darshan of the sanctified items of Shriji Maharaj and the guru parampara, expressing everyone's state of mind, he said, "We ring the bell, but along with it we ring many other things too."
It was as if Swamishri had caught the feelings in our hearts and put them into words.

The sadhus showed Mahant Swami Maharaj today's sentence placed near the murti of Pramukh Swami Maharaj. Pramukh Swami Maharaj had written: "The cause of misery is identification with the body and the sense of I and mine." Savouring it with pleasure, he came to the mandir.

After that, when Swamishri had darshan in the mandir and came to the circumambulation path, a sadhu asked, "As Swami Bapa and you have shown, the cause of misery is identification with the body and the sense of I and mine, but how can these two be removed?"
After thinking for a moment, Swamishri showed the remedy: "The glory of Bhagwan. Without it, these (identification with the body and the sense of I and mine) will never go."
